title: How do we find the angles of an isosceles trapezium?
description: In an isosceles trapezium, two right-angled triangles drawn inside it are congruent, so the two angles on one parallel side are equal. The angles on the other parallel side come from one hundred eighty minus that angle. Keeko doubts that opposite angles are equal.
teaching_notes: One idea: the two angles on the same parallel side of an isosceles trapezium are equal, and each of the other two is one hundred eighty minus it. Watch for students who give each angle the value of the angle opposite to it.

source: UVWX is an isosceles trapezium with UV || XW, UX = VW and ∠U = 65°. Find ∠V, ∠W and ∠X.
video_script.why: The child sees that the angles on one parallel side of an isosceles trapezium are equal, and the other two are 180 minus that angle.
video_script.substitution: the book's own isosceles trapezium UVWX with UV parallel to XW, UX equal to VW and angle U of 65 degrees
video_script.anchor: the isosceles trapezium UVWX of the book with perpendiculars XY and WZ
video_script.wrong_answer: angle W is sixty five degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks angle W is sixty five degrees because opposite angles are equal, but that rule belongs to a parallelogram.
video_script.payoff_line: Angle V is sixty five degrees, and angles W and X are one hundred fifteen degrees

final_answer.spoken: angle V is sixty five degrees, and angles W and X are one hundred fifteen degrees each

maths_rules: XY and WZ are perpendicular to UV; XW is parallel to UV, so XWZY has four right angles and is a rectangle; XY = WZ
triangle UXY and triangle VWZ: right angles at Y and Z, UX = VW, XY = WZ, so they are congruent by RHS
UX cuts both parallel sides, so angle X = 180 - 65 = 115; in the same way angle W = 115
video_script.design: One idea: two matching right-angled triangles make the base angles equal. One trapezium stays on the board and the two triangles are coloured in turn.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the isosceles trapezium UVWX with UV and XW marked parallel, UX and VW ticked equal, angle U of 65 degrees

marks.def: the two slanting sides are ticked as equal
marks.ang: the trapezium UVWX appears with its parallel sides marked and angle U written
marks.ask: angles V, W and X glow with question marks

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a trapezium.
<bookmark mark='def'/>When its two slanting sides are equal, it is called an isosceles trapezium.
<bookmark mark='ang'/>In isosceles trapezium U V W X, U V is parallel to X W.
Angle U is sixty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you find angles V, W and X?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two triangles that match exactly; two parallel lines cut by a slanting line with the two angles on one side joined to 180 degrees

marks.sum: the two angles on one side of a slanting line add up to one hundred eighty degrees

narration: <bookmark mark='cong'/>Triangles that match exactly are called congruent.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Between parallel lines, two angles on one side of a slanting line make one hundred eighty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Given: isosceles trapezium UVWX, UV ∥ XW, UX = VW, ∠U = 65°
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, isosceles trapezium U V W X, with U V parallel to X W.
U X equals V W, and angle U is sixty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find angles V, W and X.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: draw XY and WZ perpendicular to UV; XWZY is a rectangle, so XY = WZ

marks.draw: the lines X Y and W Z are drawn down to U V
marks.rect: the rectangle X W Z Y is coloured
marks.eq: X Y and W Z are ticked as equal

narration: <bookmark mark='draw'/>Step one, draw X Y and W Z at right angles to U V.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>X W is parallel to U V, so the other two angles are right angles too.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>X W Z Y is a rectangle, so X Y equals W Z.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: ∆UXY and ∆VWZ have right angles at Y and Z, UX = VW and XY = WZ, so ∆UXY ≅ ∆VWZ by RHS

marks.ra: the right angles at Y and Z light up
marks.hyp: U X and V W light up as equal
marks.side: X Y and W Z light up as equal

narration: <bookmark mark='ra'/>Step two, look at triangles U X Y and V W Z.
<bookmark mark='hyp'/>Each has a right angle, and the slanting sides U X and V W are equal.
<bookmark mark='side'/>The sides X Y and W Z are equal too.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>By the right angle, hypotenuse, side rule, the triangles are congruent.

marks.eq: angle U and angle V light up as equal
marks.val: sixty five degrees is written at V

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step three, matching angles of congruent triangles are equal.
<bookmark mark='val'/>Angle V equals angle U, which is sixty five degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: UX cuts both parallel sides, so ∠X = 180 − 65 = 115°, and likewise ∠W = 115°. Check: 65 + 65 + 115 + 115 = 360

marks.side: the slanting side U X lights up
marks.x: one hundred eighty minus sixty five is written at X
marks.w: one hundred fifteen degrees is written at W
marks.chk: the four angles are added to three hundred sixty

narration: <bookmark mark='side'/>Step four, the slanting side U X cuts both parallel sides.
<bookmark mark='x'/>Angle X is one hundred eighty minus sixty five, which is one hundred fifteen degrees.
<bookmark mark='w'/>In the same way, angle W is one hundred fifteen degrees.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>As a check, sixty five twice and one hundred fifteen twice make three hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Angle V is sixty five degrees, and angles W and X are one hundred fifteen degrees each.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the trapezium with 65 copied onto the corner opposite U; the slanting sides glow and lean towards each other; the copied angle is struck out

marks.doubt: sixty five is copied onto the corner opposite U
marks.lean: the slanting sides glow and lean towards each other
marks.fix: angles U and V light up as the equal pair

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks angle W is sixty five degrees, because opposite angles are equal.
<bookmark mark='lean'/>That is true in a parallelogram, but here the slanting sides lean towards each other.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The equal angles are U and V, which sit on the same parallel side.
